## Summary

Fix speculative-decoding FPM timing ownership and decode-length statistics. Each result retains its own timing span and immutable count/sum/variance instead of combining overlapped iterations or reading a missing/stale CPU length mirror. Attention-DP ranks with no local requests retain their timed dummy-forward records. Idle heartbeats now follow scheduler state, so a long forward cannot look idle merely because the publisher queue is quiet.

## Implementation

DeviceTimer exposes generic interval observers. FPM timing, schemas and publication live in `forward_pass_metrics.py`; all corresponding test cases and fixtures live in `test_forward_pass_metrics.py`, with one CPU CI registration. The DeviceTimer dependency is imported only for type checking. FPM groups existing intervals by run_batch result, preserves the same-stream check, and carries timing through rank-local PP metadata, including PREBUILT recursion, skipped output communication and the speculative-output relay. PP metadata retains both the upstream forward-time microbatch/KV snapshot and rank-local FPM timing. At _resolve_spec_v2_tokens entry, after existing result-copy synchronization and before settlement, supported EAGLE/EAGLE3/DSPARK paths freeze req.seqlen - 1 statistics on the result. Queued statistics remain a per-rank scheduler-queue snapshot and stay immutable during deferred publication.

Remove unused start/end-event fields and the unreachable monotonic fallback, inline the extra timing context manager with exception-safe sealing, remove duplicate emission-time polling, and skip per-interval elapsed-time calculations when there are no reporters. Algorithm selection is a module-level constant; shared test fixtures replace duplicate fake intervals. Full PP round-trip and skip-output regression coverage remains.

## Overhead

Production adds no CUDA events, GPU kernels, D2H transfers or explicit synchronization. FPM-off keeps the original forward method and skips decode-statistics reduction. FPM-on performs CPU bookkeeping, stream checks, statistics reduction and asynchronous publication. wall_time is the first-start/last-end span of existing instrumented intervals on one stream, including segment gaps; work outside those boundaries is excluded. The FPM v1 wire schema is unchanged. These structural checks do not quantify CPU overhead; the earlier AgentX comparisons remain in the performance-evidence comment.

## Validation

- 98 CPU tests across eight focused files passed at head `8d8616abd2778ab2c9341fbc55d664ced38449d9`, including FPM timing/publication, speculative grammar/bookkeeping, auxiliary output, PP rank offsets/DSpark relay, PP communication overlap and scheduler metrics. CPU tests stub optional compiled operators. Changed-file pre-commit and git diff --check passed. The timing regression now uses real interval completion caching and confirms active-state sampling does not consume or duplicate FPM callbacks. AST comparison confirms `forward_pass_metrics.py` (wire schema, span aggregation and publisher) matches pre-merge head `09a6cba18ec20bf4ecd621b7b8c5fc66fc7dbd37`.
- Computelab job 4285576 used two A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs, driver `595.58.03`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, `sglang-kernel==0.4.7`, and matching FlashInfer Python/cubin/JIT-cache `0.6.18` packages. The container base was amd64 digest sha256:f856a45537f82e1900ea7607edcbaa7f77fbb2e70220eae522d1d50d0046727e; full PR Python source was overlaid, and changed production-file hashes matched `9babf79d21a412f56d1a9a958d764d58dcc3464e`.
- EAGLE3 uses Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B at c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca and Nicolassuez/Qwen3-0.6B-eagle3 at `00b7c41f32655e90ee65ac5b90bb381905ce1700`. Native MTP uses Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B at `2fc06364715b967f1860aea9cf38778875588b17`.

| GPU case | Forward FPM records | Dummy records | GPU length samples | Nonempty queue checks |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| EAGLE3 / TP1 / graphs | 700 | 0 | 687 | 639 |
| EAGLE3 / attention DP2 / graphs | 2334 | 758 | 2776 | 1284 |
| EAGLE3 / attention DP2 / eager + 1.2s delay | 52 | 26 | 34 | 0 |
| No SD / attention DP2 / graphs | 3592 | 1202 | 0 | 1998 |
| Native MTP / TP1 / eager | 359 | 0 | 346 | 331 |
| EAGLE3 / attention DP2 / forced retraction | 4144 | 1311 | 2772 | 2521 |

All six cases passed. SD count/sum/population-variance matched an independent GPU-length oracle. Independently associated timing intervals matched emitted spans, bounded by separate run_batch events. Every dummy record had no scheduled requests and positive timing matching its own GPU events. Raw streams matched oracle records with no counter gaps or skipped scheduler-forward ordinals in these runs.

Asymmetric and simultaneous routed request bursts checked each rank's actual waiting queue and request ownership. The forced-retraction case additionally checked 525/521 queued-decode snapshots on ranks 0/1. Scheduler-driven idle heartbeat checks found no busy-period violations, including repeated 1.2-second forward delays; receipt-time checks exclude 100 ms around state transitions for IPC delivery latency, complemented by deterministic publisher-state unit tests.

GPU coverage is aggregated PP1 with TP1 / attention DP2; PP and unsupported SD algorithms retain their stated validation boundaries. Initial environment/coverage setup attempts are excluded from the six-case matrix and retained in the experiment records.

Merged main `efb62ce269b499123e2d1c89005ee4cea8c31098`. The scheduler active-event timestamp API and cached device-event state are retained alongside FPM idle-heartbeat gating and interval observers. The GPU results above belong to head `9babf79d21a412f56d1a9a958d764d58dcc3464e` on main `5c2de3f35567ffceec6cea86ba18e075692e9101`; GPU tests were not rerun for the current head. PP speculative-relay coverage in this update is CPU-only. The recorded GPU allocation exited 0:0 with no remaining GPU processes.

[Full B300 experiment log](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aisimulate/blob/3205e79f2b422610d8b5855ccefc3d835d06bb68/docs/experiments/agentx-deepseek-v4-pro-440845-b300-slurm/README.md).

### Interpretation and limitations

- Total throughput changed **-0.77% (B200)** and **-0.65% (B300)**; output throughput changed **-0.33%** and **-0.49%**. Latency changes vary by percentile. One historical comparison and one ordered pair do not establish zero overhead or a statistical overhead bound; closed-loop runs complete slightly different request sets.
- Both experiments' measured exports report `submission_valid=true` and zero request errors/output-length mismatches. B300 had **3/4 profiling cancellations** at the drain deadline. Its off warmup exported **353 successes plus one empty-content response error**, although the phase progress log counted 354 completed with zero errors; on warmup exported 354 successes and omitted the error-count metric.
- B300 needed a guarded forkserver cleanup during each dataset setup, before measurement. No engine/client source or serving setting was changed. Optional persistent mmap-cache writes failed, while the complete runtime mmap and replay succeeded.
- FPM-on Prometheus exports reported counter-reset warnings whose cause remains unresolved. Affected Prometheus delta/rate statistics are not used in these tables; native FPM counters showed no resets. Observable counter continuity does not rule out drops before sequence assignment.

## AgentX FPM-off/on performance evidence

Adding the two completed experiments below. The FPM-enabled runs use a compatibility backport of this PR at `ed18d64951b93ac252d921ee037ce0d3327eda1f` onto SGLang `71de97b264b04dcd514cf904003028aefe9775c8` (shared amd64 image digest `sha256:f856a45537f82e1900ea7607edcbaa7f77fbb2e70220eae522d1d50d0046727e`). This provides pinned-runtime performance evidence; it does not replace full PR-head integration or PP GPU validation.

Both experiments replay all 393 AgentX Weka trajectories, seed 42, with a 3600-second measured sending phase, GPU prefix caching and HiCache disabled. FPM-on includes the external buffered recorder. Tables use final client request exports, retain their drain windows, and calculate `100 * (on / off - 1)` from unrounded values. Total throughput includes cached prompt tokens. Speculative acceptance is simulated, so these are performance tests, not model-quality tests.

### 1. GLM-5.2 NVFP4 — 8×B200, TP8/EP1, PP1, no attention DP, c4

Dynamo frontend + SGLang, EAGLE/native MTP (3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens), simulated acceptance length 2.99.

**Historical comparison:** FPM-off job `4187044` versus FPM-on job `4208956`, on different B200 nodes. The off run used the original nightly; the on run used the FPM-fixed image. Resolved client dependencies also differ. These are not a same-node, same-runtime A/B pair.
